clue.text: Unusual rig of a singing barber

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some odd rigging belonging to a barber who sings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' is the anagram signal: RIG OF A rearranged makes the barber of Rossini's and Mozart's operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro is the barber hero of Rossini's opera The Barber of Seville, who sings the famous 'Largo al factotum'.

clue.text: Raphael's famous works in empty boxes

indicators.note: the word in tells us the empty letter sits inside the boxes

parts.note: cartons are cardboard boxes
empty means nothing, the letter O standing for zero

explanation.surface: Raphael's celebrated pictures stored away in empty packing boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Raphael Cartoons are full-size designs for tapestries, kept in the V&A in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael's tapestry designs for the Sistine Chapel are known as the Raphael Cartoons, cartoon being the term for a full-size preparatory drawing.

clue.text: Tchaikovsky's arrangement of a trick tune: sucre

indicators.note: an arrangement of music reorders it, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Tchaikovsky rearranges some odd tune with a sugary French name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement of' signals the anagram of A TRICK TUNE SUCRE; the definition is just the possessive 'Tchaikovsky's', meaning one of his works. 'Sucre' (French for sugar) nods to the Sugar Plum Fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballet suite famous as one of the Russian composer's best-loved works, including the Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy.

clue.text: Mass introduction French king gets in Manx race

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: gets is read as takes in, so the Manx race with in before it receives the king

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A French monarch enters the Isle of Man motorbike race to open the Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' means takes in: the Manx race with 'in' before it takes the French king between its two letters. 'Manx race' is the Isle of Man TT.
explanation.definitionFit: The introit is the opening chant or psalm sung at the start of a Catholic Mass.

clue.text: Give anything but thanks to a benefactor

definitions.text: Give anything but thanks to a benefactor

parts.words: Give anything but thanks to a benefactor
parts.note: read literally, to give anything other than gratitude to someone who helped you is to display a lack of thankfulness

explanation.definitionFit: Displaying ungratefulness, the opposite of thanking someone, is precisely giving a benefactor anything but thanks.

clue.text: Naval dockyard in the pink for the most part

parts.note: rosy means pink in colour

indicators.note: most of the word the is kept, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A naval dockyard mostly in the pink of health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the pink' looks like one idiom, but 'pink' gives ROSY and 'the', with 'for the most part' cutting its last letter, gives TH; 'in' is a link. ROSYTH is a naval base in Fife, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosyth on the Firth of Forth in Scotland is a long-standing Royal Navy dockyard.

clue.text: Items from all quarters

parts.note: reports gathered from every point of the compass, whose initials are North, East, West and South

explanation.walkthrough: The four compass points' initials, N E W S, spell the word, a well-known folk etymology.
explanation.definitionFit: Reported items gathered from everywhere: the compass points North, East, West, South give its letters.

clue.text: Sorted mail in the capital

indicators.note: post that is sorted is put into a new order, so the letters of mail are rearranged

explanation.surface: Post sorted in the capital city's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted' is the anagram signal on MAIL; 'the capital' is a capital city, here Peru's.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Vessel turned out for Mr Heath

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Vessel turned out for Mr Heath (3)'; URN must be RUN turned round, but no reading of 'out for Mr Heath' gives RUN without a guess, and a search finds no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: Vessel turned out for Mr Heath

clue.text: Rugby player at sea gets a smack

definitions.meaning: the player in the front row of the scrum who hooks the ball back
a smack is a small sailing fishing boat; a similar single-masted fishing vessel

explanation.surface: A rugby forward who goes to sea and gets slapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' looks like a blow, but at sea it is a small fishing boat, and a hooker is another such boat.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a scrum position in rugby; the other is a traditional one-masted fishing boat, like a smack.

clue.text: Move to perform in less than a second

indicators.note: the word in places the performing inside the shortened second
less than the whole word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a very short time
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: A chess move made in under a second.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK (a second) loses its last letter by 'less than' to give TIC, and ACT goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned move or manoeuvre made to achieve an aim.

clue.text: My word, is there a disturbance!

definitions.text: My word, is there a disturbance!

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters of my word is are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at some commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: MY WORD IS rearranged, with 'disturbance' as the signal, while the whole clue describes rowdy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdyism is noisy, disorderly behaviour, the kind of commotion that prompts such an exclamation.

clue.text: Occasional seat over a stone .

parts.note: an 'occasional' seat is one used only for a particular occasion; this one stands over a famous stone

explanation.walkthrough: The chair in Westminster Abbey used at every crowning was built to hold the Stone of Scone beneath its seat.
explanation.definitionFit: St Edward's Chair, used only at crownings, was made to house the Stone of Scone under the seat.

clue.text: Charge transmitted through the national grid

indicators.note: the answer is passed along inside the words that follow, spanning part of national

explanation.surface: Electric charge sent through the National Grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters sit inside 'national'; the surface about electricity distracts from the extraction.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electric charge.

clue.text: Abandon wrecked old boats in 'enemy hands

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Abandon wrecked old boats in 'enemy hands (7)'; the parse puts ARKS (old boats) jumbled by 'wrecked' inside FOE, an anagram of a synonym that the check refuses
annotationWithheld.clue: Abandon wrecked old boats in 'enemy hands

clue.text: Scandinavian coin or note

parts.note: taken as written
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is a Scandinavian coin or a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a banknote beside 'coin', but it is the musical note E.
explanation.definitionFit: The öre is a small coin, a hundredth of a krona, in Sweden, and of a krone in Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: Sailing ship and plunderer

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailing ship and the pirate who robs from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, a member of a gang that robs travellers.

clue.text: A sucker for ladybirds?

parts.note: a sucker is an insect that sucks plant sap, and also someone easily taken in; here it is food for ladybirds

explanation.definitionFit: Aphids suck sap from plants and are the main prey of ladybirds.

clue.text: Ropy home decorator?

definitions.meaning: a rope sense: on a boat the ... is the rope at the bow for tying up

explanation.surface: A poor-quality house decorator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ropy' reads as British slang for shoddy, but here it points to the rope sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the line used to moor a small boat; the other is a tradesman who paints walls.

clue.text: Lamb's fruitful but unstable companion

parts.note: a wobbly fruit preserve served alongside roast lamb, sounding like a description of a person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Companion' suggests a person (or Charles Lamb's friend), but it is the sweet accompaniment to roast lamb: made of fruit, and wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: This set preserve of small red berries is traditionally served with roast lamb, and it wobbles.

clue.text: Decay that is breaking up vehicles

indicators.note: the abbreviation splits the vehicles into two parts by sitting inside them

parts.note: cars are vehicles
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Rot that causes vehicles to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' looks like an anagram signal, but IE breaks into CARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical name for decay of teeth or bone.

clue.text: Hardy associate crowned with honour …

definitions.meaning: Stan ... was the partner of Oliver Hardy in the comedy double act
a wreath of bay leaves crowning a victor is a mark of honour

explanation.surface: A partner of Hardy crowned with distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests the novelist (as in the next clue), but it is Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy; 'crowned with' joins the wreath sense.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is Stan, Oliver Hardy's comedy partner; the other is a bay wreath, an emblem of distinction.

clue.text: Begin with 9 for a top performance

parts.note: to start is to begin
the answer to clue 9, a vessel

explanation.surface: Opening with number nine to give the best act.
explanation.walkthrough: A star turn is the main act on a variety bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the leading act or most impressive performance in a show.

clue.text: … sets out to find a Hardy

indicators.note: out signals the letters of sets are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Sets out to track down a Hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Hardy' means a Hardy novel, Tess of the d'Urbervilles, linking to the previous clue's comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles is often called simply by its heroine's name.

clue.text: Tasty bit of footwear

parts.note: a flap on a shoe under the laces that shares its name with a cooked meat dish

explanation.definitionFit: The flap under a shoe's laces has the same name as the muscular mouth organ, served as cold meat.

clue.text: Awkward stance for the climb

indicators.note: an awkward stance is badly arranged, so its letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An awkward posture for going up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' is the anagram signal on STANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb, the act of going up.

clue.text: Start endeavour-and stop it

indicators.note: the start of the word endeavour supplies its opening three letters

explanation.surface: Begin a task and then give it up.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening three letters of 'endeavour' give the answer; 'and' and 'it' link to the definition 'stop'.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to bring it to a halt, to finish it.

clue.text: Sort of life beloved of old

indicators.note: sort here means arrange, so the letters of life are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of life cherished in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' reads as 'kind of', but is the anagram signal on LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lief is an archaic word meaning dear or gladly, as in 'I would as lief'.
